recipes.description: The original cocktail: whiskey, sugar, bitters, water.
recipes.notes: Stir with ice about 20 seconds — you want dilution and chill without clouding. Express the orange twist over the drink before dropping it in.
steps: Add simple syrup (or sugar cube + water) and bitters to a rocks glass.
Add bourbon and a large ice cube.
Stir 20 seconds until chilled and diluted.
Express an orange twist over the glass and drop it in.
recipes.title: Old Fashioned

recipes.description: Rye, sweet vermouth, and bitters — the Manhattan's drier, spicier soul.
recipes.notes: Use a decent sweet vermouth and keep it refrigerated once opened. Rye is traditional; bourbon makes a sweeter Manhattan.
steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir 20–30 seconds until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a cherry.
recipes.title: Manhattan

recipes.description: Whiskey's answer to the Negroni: bourbon, Campari, sweet vermouth.
recipes.notes: Equal-parts (1 oz each) also works and is closer to the original 1927 spec — try both and pick your ratio.
steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir 20 seconds until chilled.
Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass.
Express an orange twist over the glass and drop it in.
recipes.title: Boulevardier

recipes.description: Bright and frothy — lemon and bourbon with a silky cap.
recipes.notes: Skip the egg white if you prefer; the drink is still excellent. Dry-shake (no ice) first if using egg white, then shake with ice.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker (no ice if using egg white) and shake 10 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass, or into a coupe without ice.
recipes.title: Whiskey Sour

recipes.description: Crisp, cold, and brutally simple. The king of cocktails.
recipes.notes: Stir, don't shake — shaking clouds it and over-dilutes. Keep gin and glassware cold; vermouth goes in the fridge after opening.
steps: Chill a coupe or martini glass.
Add gin and vermouth to a mixing glass with plenty of ice.
Stir 20–30 seconds until ice-cold.
Strain into the chilled glass.
Express a lemon twist over the drink, or drop in an olive.
recipes.title: Dry Martini

recipes.description: Equal parts gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth. Bitter, bold, perfect.
recipes.notes: Built in the glass works fine — no mixing glass required. A Negroni Sbagliato swaps the gin for prosecco.
steps: Add all ingredients to a rocks glass with a large ice cube.
Stir briefly to chill and combine.
Express an orange twist over the glass and drop it in.
recipes.title: Negroni

recipes.description: Gin, tonic, ice, citrus — simplicity done right.
recipes.notes: Use plenty of ice and cold tonic — a warm, flat G&T is a sad thing. Fever-Tree or Q are reliable tonics.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add gin.
Top with chilled tonic and stir once gently.
Garnish with a lime wedge.
recipes.title: Gin & Tonic

recipes.description: Rum, lime, sugar. Nothing to hide behind — balance is everything.
recipes.notes: The test of a good rum and fresh limes. Adjust syrup a touch to taste — limes vary.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lime wheel.
recipes.title: Daiquiri

recipes.description: Mint, lime, rum, and fizz — the Cuban cooler.
recipes.notes: Muddle mint gently — press, don't shred, or it turns bitter. Slap the garnish mint between your palms to release aroma.
steps: Gently muddle mint with lime juice and syrup in a highball glass.
Add rum and fill with crushed ice.
Top with club soda and stir briefly.
Garnish with a mint sprig.
recipes.title: Mojito

recipes.description: The tiki classic: aged rum, lime, curaçao, and orgeat.

ingredients.item: Aged rum (Jamaican-style if you have it)

recipes.notes: 1944 Trader Vic's spec. Orgeat is the soul of the drink — don't skip it.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake 10 seconds.
Strain over crushed ice in a rocks glass.
Garnish with mint and the spent lime shell.
recipes.title: Mai Tai

recipes.description: Tequila, lime, orange liqueur, salt. Sunshine in a glass.
recipes.notes: Fresh lime juice only — never sour mix. Salt half the rim so drinkers can choose.
steps: Salt the rim of a rocks glass if desired; fill with ice.
Add tequila, lime juice, and orange liqueur to a shaker with ice.
Shake 10–12 seconds.
Strain into the glass and garnish with a lime wheel.
recipes.title: Margarita

recipes.description: Tequila and grapefruit soda — Mexico's actual favorite highball.
recipes.notes: A pinch of salt in the drink itself (not just the rim) sharpens everything.
steps: Salt the rim of a highball glass if desired; fill with ice.
Add tequila and lime juice.
Top with grapefruit soda and stir gently.
Garnish with a grapefruit wedge.
recipes.title: Paloma

recipes.description: Vodka, cranberry, lime, orange — the '90s icon, done properly.
recipes.notes: It should be pale pink, not red — go easy on the cranberry.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express a lime twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Cosmopolitan

recipes.description: Vodka, espresso, coffee liqueur — dessert and a nightcap in one.
recipes.notes: Shake hard — the foam cap is the whole point. Fresh espresso matters; cold brew works in a pinch.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with plenty of ice.
Shake hard 12–15 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Float 3 coffee beans on the foam.
recipes.title: Espresso Martini

recipes.description: Vodka, lime, and spicy ginger beer in a copper mug.
recipes.notes: Ginger beer, not ginger ale — you want the bite. The copper mug is tradition, not requirement.
steps: Fill a copper mug or highball with ice.
Add vodka and lime juice.
Top with ginger beer and stir gently.
Garnish with a lime wheel.
recipes.title: Moscow Mule

recipes.description: Bitter orange, prosecco, and soda — Italy's golden hour.
recipes.notes: 3-2-1: prosecco, Aperol, soda. Build over ice in the glass — no shaker needed.
steps: Fill a wine glass with ice.
Add prosecco, then Aperol, then soda.
Stir once gently and garnish with an orange slice.
recipes.title: Aperol Spritz

recipes.description: Rye, Peychaud's bitters, and an absinthe rinse — New Orleans in a glass.
recipes.notes: Rinse a chilled rocks glass with absinthe and discard the excess. Traditionalists express the lemon twist over the drink and discard it.
steps: Rinse a chilled rocks glass with absinthe; discard excess.
Stir rye, syrup, and bitters with ice 20 seconds.
Strain into the prepared glass.
Express a lemon twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Sazerac

recipes.description: Bourbon, mint, and crushed ice in a frosty silver cup.
recipes.notes: Pack the cup tight with crushed ice — the frost on the outside is the point. Use a straw cut short so you get the mint aroma with every sip.
steps: Gently muddle mint with syrup in a julep cup.
Add bourbon and pack tightly with crushed ice.
Stir briefly and top with more crushed ice.
Garnish with a mint sprig and a short straw.
recipes.title: Mint Julep

recipes.description: Hot coffee, Irish whiskey, brown sugar, and a cold cream float.
recipes.glass: Heatproof mug or Irish coffee glass
recipes.notes: Whip the cream just to soft peaks and pour it over the back of a spoon so it floats. Drink through the cold cream.
steps: Warm the glass with hot water; discard.
Add brown sugar and hot coffee; stir to dissolve.
Stir in the whiskey.
Float the cream over the back of a spoon.
recipes.title: Irish Coffee

recipes.description: A Manhattan made with Scotch — smoky, smooth, and elegant.
recipes.notes: A peaty single malt makes a bolder Rob Roy; blended Scotch keeps it smooth. Perfect Manhattan specs apply.
steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir 20–30 seconds until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a cherry or lemon twist.
recipes.title: Rob Roy

recipes.description: Smoky Scotch, ginger-honey, and lemon with a peaty float.
recipes.notes: Honey-ginger syrup: simmer equal parts honey and water with sliced ginger 10 minutes, then strain. The Islay float goes on last — don't stir it in.
steps: Shake blended Scotch, lemon, and honey-ginger syrup with ice 10 seconds.
Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass.
Float the Islay Scotch on top.
Garnish with candied ginger.
recipes.title: Penicillin

recipes.description: Bourbon, honey, and lemon — a Whiskey Sour in a gold jacket.
recipes.notes: Use 2:1 honey syrup so it mixes easily and the drink isn't too sweet. No egg white needed here.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
Express a lemon twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Gold Rush

recipes.description: Equal parts bourbon, Aperol, amaro, and lemon — bitter, bright, balanced.
recipes.notes: Equal parts makes it foolproof. Amaro Nonino is traditional; another mild amaro works in a pinch.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipes.title: Paper Plane

recipes.description: Rye meets cognac in this rich New Orleans stirred classic.
recipes.notes: Pronounced 'voo ka-RAY'. The two bitters plus Bénédictine give it a complexity that rewards slow sipping.
steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir 25–30 seconds until well chilled.
Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass.
Garnish with a cherry and lemon twist.
recipes.title: Vieux Carré

recipes.description: Bourbon muddled with mint and lemon — a Julep's rougher cousin.
recipes.notes: Muddle the mint gently with the lemon and syrup, then shake it all — straining keeps the texture clean.
steps: Gently muddle mint with lemon juice and syrup in a shaker.
Add bourbon and ice; shake 10 seconds.
Strain over crushed ice in a rocks glass.
Garnish with a mint sprig.
recipes.title: Whiskey Smash

recipes.description: Whiskey, honey, lemon, and hot water — the cold-weather cure-all.
recipes.notes: Dissolve the honey in a splash of hot water first so it doesn't sink. A cinnamon stick stirrer is a welcome addition.
steps: Add honey to a warm mug with a splash of hot water; stir to dissolve.
Add whiskey and lemon juice.
Top with hot water and stir.
Garnish with a clove-studded lemon wheel.
recipes.title: Hot Toddy

recipes.description: Scotch and Drambuie — two ingredients, all warmth.
recipes.notes: Stir it down a little or serve over a large cube — it opens up beautifully with dilution.
steps: Add both to a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
Stir briefly to combine and chill.
Express a lemon twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Rusty Nail

recipes.description: Scotch, cherry, vermouth, and orange — the name says it all.
recipes.notes: Equal parts, so it's easy to remember. Fresh orange juice is essential — bottled juice dulls it.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express an orange twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Blood & Sand

recipes.description: Gin, lemon, and fizz over ice — tall, tart, and timeless.
recipes.notes: The namesake of the great 1874 hoax. Any Collins glass works; keep the soda cold and lively.
steps: Fill a Collins glass with ice.
Add gin, lemon, and syrup; stir briefly.
Top with club soda.
Garnish with a lemon wheel and cherry.
recipes.title: Tom Collins

recipes.description: Gin, lemon, and champagne — celebration in a flute.
recipes.notes: Named for the WWI field gun — it hits like one if you're careless. Cognac swaps in for gin in the older French style.
steps: Shake gin, lemon, and syrup with ice 10 seconds.
Strain into a flute.
Top with chilled champagne.
Express a lemon twist over the drink.
recipes.title: French 75

recipes.description: Gin, honey, and lemon — Prohibition's sweetest workaround.
recipes.notes: Honey was the Prohibition-era mask for rough gin. With good gin today, it's just delicious.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express a lemon twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Bee's Knees

recipes.description: Gin and lime, ice-cold — the sailor's remedy.
recipes.notes: Rose's lime cordial is the naval original; fresh lime and syrup is the modern craft standard. Both are correct.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lime wheel.
recipes.title: Gimlet

recipes.description: Equal parts gin, Chartreuse, maraschino, and lime — a green revelation.
recipes.notes: A 1920s Detroit Athletic Club recipe revived in Seattle. Equal parts — impossible to forget, impossible not to love.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipes.title: Last Word

recipes.description: The hair-of-the-dog classic: gin, citrus, and a whisper of absinthe.
recipes.notes: Harry Craddock's warning stands: 'Four of these taken in swift succession will unrevive the corpse again.'
steps: Rinse a chilled coupe with absinthe; discard excess.
Shake remaining ingredients with ice 10 seconds.
Strain into the prepared coupe.
Express an orange twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Corpse Reviver #2

recipes.description: Gin, raspberry, lemon, and a silky egg-white cap.
recipes.notes: Dry-shake (no ice) first for maximum foam, then shake with ice. Raspberry syrup: simmer raspberries with equal sugar and water, strain.
steps: Dry-shake all ingredients without ice 10 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with raspberries.
recipes.title: Clover Club

recipes.description: Gin, violet, and maraschino — the sky-blue classic.
recipes.notes: The crème de violette gives the pale blue hue — go easy, it's potent. Some recipes skip it; don't.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a cherry.
recipes.title: Aviation

recipes.description: Gin sour crowned with a bleeding float of blackberry liqueur.
recipes.notes: Dick Bradsell's 1980s London creation. Pour the crème de mûre over the top last so it bleeds down through the ice.
steps: Shake gin, lemon, and syrup with ice 10 seconds.
Strain over crushed ice in a rocks glass.
Float crème de mûre over the top.
Garnish with a blackberry and lemon slice.
recipes.title: Bramble

recipes.description: The Raffles Hotel legend — fruity, pink, and deceptively complex.
recipes.notes: Many ingredients, one unmistakable pink result. Shake everything except the soda, then top.
steps: Shake all ingredients except soda with ice 10 seconds.
Strain into a hurricane glass over fresh ice.
Top with club soda.
Garnish with pineapple and a cherry.
recipes.title: Singapore Sling

recipes.description: A Mojito's gin twin — mint, lime, and a silky chill.
recipes.notes: Named for Chicago's South Side. Shake the mint with everything and fine-strain for a clean, green-gold drink.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a mint sprig.
recipes.title: Southside

recipes.description: Bond's order: gin, vodka, and Kina Lillet — shaken, not stirred.

ingredients.item: Lillet Blanc (in place of Kina Lillet)

recipes.notes: From Casino Royale. Lillet Blanc stands in for the discontinued Kina Lillet. It is unapologetically strong.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake 10–12 seconds until ice-cold.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express a large lemon twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Vesper

recipes.description: Gin and sweet vermouth with a Fernet Branca bite.
recipes.notes: Ada Coleman's Savoy creation. The Fernet is just two dashes — it seasons the drink without taking over.
steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir 20–30 seconds until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express an orange twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Hanky Panky

recipes.description: The Martini's ancestor: Old Tom gin, vermouth, and maraschino.
recipes.notes: Sweeter and rounder than a Martini. Old Tom gin is traditional; London dry makes a drier, more modern version.
steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir 25 seconds until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express a lemon twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Martinez

recipes.description: Dark rum and ginger beer with lime — Bermuda's national drink.

ingredients.item: Dark rum (Goslings Black Seal is traditional)

recipes.notes: Float the rum on top of the ginger beer for the storm-cloud look. Goslings trademarked the name — with their rum, it's official.
steps: Fill a highball with ice.
Add ginger beer and lime juice.
Float the rum on top.
Garnish with a lime wedge.
recipes.title: Dark 'n' Stormy

recipes.description: Rum, coconut, and pineapple, blended frosty.

ingredients.item: Cream of coconut (such as Coco López)

recipes.notes: Puerto Rico's official drink since 1978. Blend with ice until smooth — a shaker works if you don't want to drag out the blender.
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender with a cup of ice.
Blend until smooth.
Pour into a hurricane glass.
Garnish with pineapple and a cherry.
recipes.title: Piña Colada

recipes.description: Two rums, passion fruit, and citrus — the French Quarter hurricane.
recipes.notes: Pat O'Brien's New Orleans original. Passion fruit syrup (not juice) gives it the signature color and depth.
steps: Shake all ingredients with ice 10 seconds.
Strain over crushed ice in a hurricane glass.
Garnish with an orange slice and cherry.
recipes.title: Hurricane

recipes.description: The legendary tiki powerhouse — three rums, fruit, and fire.
recipes.notes: Donn Beach's 1934 creation allegedly limited customers to two. Respect the legend.
steps: Blend all ingredients with crushed ice 5 seconds.
Pour unstrained into a tiki mug.
Top with more crushed ice.
Garnish with mint.
recipes.title: Zombie

recipes.description: Dark rum meets Campari and pineapple — bitter tiki at its best.
recipes.notes: From the Aviary bar in Kuala Lumpur. The rare tiki drink where bitter leads — Campari and pineapple are made for each other.
steps: Shake all ingredients with ice 10 seconds.
Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
Garnish with pineapple fronds.
recipes.title: Jungle Bird

recipes.description: Rum, pineapple, orange, and coconut under a snowy nutmeg cap.
recipes.notes: Born at the Soggy Dollar Bar in the British Virgin Islands. The nutmeg grating on top is non-negotiable.
steps: Shake all ingredients with ice 10 seconds.
Strain over fresh ice in a hurricane glass.
Grate fresh nutmeg generously over the top.
recipes.title: Painkiller

recipes.description: Tequila and orange juice sunrise-striped with grenadine.
recipes.notes: Pour the grenadine last and don't stir — it sinks and creates the sunrise gradient.
steps: Fill a highball with ice.
Add tequila and orange juice.
Slowly pour grenadine down the inside of the glass.
Garnish with orange and a cherry.
recipes.title: Tequila Sunrise

recipes.description: Tequila, Campari, grapefruit, and lime — a bitter Paloma with ambition.
recipes.notes: Katie Stipe's modern classic. The Campari turns a simple tequila sour into something brooding and complex.
steps: Shake all ingredients with ice 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express a grapefruit twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Siesta

recipes.description: An Old Fashioned built on reposado and mezcal with agave.
recipes.notes: Phil Ward's modern classic. The mezcal is a seasoning — just enough smoke to haunt the reposado.
steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir 20–25 seconds until well chilled.
Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass.
Express an orange twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Oaxaca Old Fashioned

recipes.description: Tequila, lime, and sparkling mineral water — Texas's minimalist cooler.
recipes.notes: Topo Chico is traditional, but any aggressively carbonated mineral water works. No sweetener — that's the point.
steps: Fill a highball with ice.
Add tequila and lime juice.
Top with chilled Topo Chico.
Garnish with a lime wedge.
recipes.title: Ranch Water

recipes.description: Vodka and spiced tomato — brunch's savory champion.
recipes.notes: Roll (pour back and forth between tins) rather than shaking — shaking makes tomato juice foamy. Season boldly; tomato needs it.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice.
Roll by pouring between two tins to mix and chill.
Strain into a highball over fresh ice.
Garnish with celery and a lemon wedge.
recipes.title: Bloody Mary

recipes.description: Vodka, coffee liqueur, and cream — dessert in a rocks glass.
recipes.notes: Float the cream on top for the classic layered look, then let the drinker stir. The Dude abides.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice.
Add vodka and coffee liqueur; stir briefly.
Float the cream over the top.
recipes.title: White Russian

recipes.description: Vodka and coffee liqueur, no cream — darker and drier.
recipes.notes: The White Russian's leaner sibling. A touch of cola on top is an old-school variation.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice.
Add both ingredients and stir briefly.
recipes.title: Black Russian

recipes.description: Vodka, cranberry, and grapefruit — crisp and breezy.
recipes.notes: Its 1980s siblings: the Bay Breeze (pineapple instead of grapefruit) and the Madras (orange instead of cranberry).
steps: Fill a highball with ice.
Add all ingredients and stir gently.
Garnish with a lime wedge.
recipes.title: Sea Breeze

recipes.description: Vodka, lemon, and a sugared rim — sweet-tart and dangerous.
recipes.notes: Rim half the coupe with sugar so drinkers can choose. It should taste like the candy, grown up.
steps: Sugar the rim of a chilled coupe (half-rim recommended).
Shake all ingredients with ice 10–12 seconds.
Strain into the prepared coupe.
Express a lemon twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Lemon Drop

recipes.description: Campari, sweet vermouth, and soda — the Negroni's lighter ancestor.
recipes.notes: The first drink Bond ever orders in the novels. Add the soda last to keep the fizz lively.
steps: Fill a highball with ice.
Add Campari and vermouth; stir briefly.
Top with chilled club soda.
Garnish with an orange slice.
recipes.title: Americano

recipes.description: A Negroni lengthened with prosecco — lighter, bubblier, just as bitter.
recipes.notes: 'Sbagliato' means mistaken — legend says a bartender grabbed prosecco instead of gin. The mistake stuck.
steps: Fill a glass with ice.
Add Campari and vermouth; stir briefly.
Top with chilled prosecco.
Garnish with an orange slice.
recipes.title: Negroni Sbagliato

recipes.description: Cognac, orange liqueur, and lemon — the sour that started them all.
recipes.notes: Sugar half the rim for the classic presentation. Named for the motorcycle sidecar — supposedly the preferred ride of its inventor.
steps: Sugar half the rim of a chilled coupe.
Shake all ingredients with ice 10–12 seconds.
Strain into the prepared coupe.
Express an orange twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Sidecar

recipes.description: Champagne and blackcurrant — dark, elegant, and effortless.
recipes.notes: Cassis first, then champagne — the bubbles do the mixing. The still-wine version is just a Kir.
steps: Pour cassis into a flute.
Top slowly with chilled champagne.
recipes.title: Kir Royale

recipes.description: Prosecco and white peach purée — Venice in a flute.
recipes.notes: Harry's Bar, Venice, 1948. White peaches are traditional; yellow work but change the color. Keep everything cold.
steps: Pour chilled peach purée into a flute.
Top slowly with chilled prosecco, stirring gently as you pour.
recipes.title: Bellini

recipes.description: Half champagne, half orange juice — brunch's official drink.
recipes.notes: Juice first or champagne first — bartenders argue endlessly. Cold ingredients and a gentle hand matter more.
steps: Pour chilled orange juice into a flute.
Top slowly with chilled champagne.
recipes.title: Mimosa

recipes.description: Pisco, lime, and a cloud of egg white with bitters on top.
recipes.notes: Peru and Chile both claim it. Dry-shake first for the foam cap, then dot bitters on top in a simple pattern.
steps: Dry-shake all ingredients except bitters without ice 10 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Dot bitters on the foam.
recipes.title: Pisco Sour

recipes.description: Cachaça muddled with lime and sugar — Brazil's national cocktail.
recipes.notes: Muddle the lime and sugar firmly to release the oils from the peel — that's where the flavor lives. Pronounced 'kai-purr-EEN-ya'.
steps: Muddle lime wedges and sugar firmly in a rocks glass.
Fill with crushed ice.
Add cachaça and stir well.
Garnish with a lime wedge.
recipes.title: Caipirinha

recipes.description: Amaretto and lemon with a bourbon backbone — the sour, perfected.
recipes.notes: Jeffrey Morgenthaler's spec: the bourbon keeps the amaretto from going candy-sweet. Egg white makes it silky.
steps: Dry-shake all ingredients without ice 10 seconds (if using egg white).
Add ice and shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
Garnish with a cherry and orange slice.
recipes.title: Amaretto Sour
